title: Elevator Floors Travelled
description: An elevator starts at floor `s` and visits the floors in `a` in the given order. Return the total number of floors it travels.

title: Rejected Parking Arrivals
description: A car park holds at most `cap` cars. Each event in `events` is `1` (a car arrives) or `-1` (a parked car leaves). An arrival when the car park is full is turned away and never enters. A departure only happens when at least one car is parked. Return how many arrivals were turned away.
constraints: events[i] is 1 or -1 and a departure never happens in an empty car park

title: Overdraft Event Count
description: An account starts at `0`. Each value of `a` is a deposit (positive) or withdrawal (negative) applied in order. Return how many times, right after a transaction, the balance is below zero.

title: Switches On After Flips
description: `n` switches numbered `0..n-1` all start off. Every entry of `flips` toggles that switch. Return how many switches are on at the end.

title: Elements After Last Maximum
description: Return how many elements of `a` come after the last occurrence of its largest value.

title: Prefix Majority Index
description: All values of `a` are non-negative. Return the smallest index `i` such that the sum of `a[0..i]` is more than half of the total sum of `a`, or `-1` if the total is `0`.

examples.explanation: The prefix first passes half at index 2.
The prefix first passes half at index 0.

title: Odd Even Position Difference
description: Return (sum of the elements at even indices `0, 2, 4, ...`) minus (sum of the elements at odd indices) of `a`.

title: Pairs Of Socks Count
description: Each value in `a` is the colour code of one sock. Two socks of the same colour form a pair and a sock is used in at most one pair. Return the largest number of pairs that can be made.

title: Min Max Position Distance
description: Let `i` be the index of the first occurrence of the smallest value of `a` and `j` the index of the first occurrence of its largest value. Return `|i - j|`.

title: Triple Median Total
description: For every three consecutive elements of `a`, take their median (the middle value after sorting). Return the sum of these medians over all `a.length - 2` triples.

title: Zero Sum Prefix Count
description: Return how many non-empty prefixes of `a` have a sum of exactly `0`.

title: Equal Even Split Count
description: A split point `i` (`1 <= i < a.length`) cuts `a` into `a[0..i-1]` and `a[i..]`. Return the number of split points where both parts contain the same number of even values.

title: Hop Count To Exit
description: You stand on index `0` of `a`. From index `i` you hop `a[i]` places to the right. Return how many hops are needed until you land beyond the last index.

title: Bouncing Ball Position
description: A ball starts at position `0` on a line segment `[0, L]` and moves `1` unit per second to the right. When it reaches `L` it turns around and moves left, and when it reaches `0` it turns around again. Return its position after `t` seconds.

examples.explanation: After 3 is the answer; the ball is at position 3.
After 3 is the answer; the ball is at position 3.

title: Largest Divisible Element
description: Return the largest element of `a` that is divisible by `k`, or `-1` if no element is.

title: Tank Overflow Total
description: A tank of capacity `cap` starts empty. Each value of `flow` is the net change in litres for one hour. The level cannot go below `0`, and any water above `cap` is lost. Return the total litres lost over all hours.

title: Rank Of First Element
description: Return the 1-based position `a[0]` would have if `a` were sorted in non-decreasing order, placing it before any other element equal to it (that is, one more than the number of elements strictly smaller than `a[0]`).

title: Pangram Check
description: `s` contains lowercase letters and spaces. Return `true` if every letter from `a` to `z` appears at least once in `s`.

examples.input: s = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"

constraints: s has only lowercase letters and spaces

args: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
a quick movement of the enemy will jeopardize six gunboats
pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs

title: Sum Of Embedded Numbers
description: `s` mixes lowercase letters and digits. Each maximal block of consecutive digits is one number. Return the sum of all these numbers (`0` if there are none).
constraints: s has lowercase letters and digits; every digit block has at most 9 digits

title: Distinct Digit Kinds
description: Return how many different digit values (`0`-`9`) appear in the decimal form of `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Mirror Number Difference
description: Let `rev(n)` be `n` with its decimal digits reversed (trailing zeros of `n` become leading zeros and vanish). Return `|n - rev(n)|`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Triangle Type Code
description: Given three side lengths, return `0` if they cannot form a triangle with positive area, `1` if the triangle is equilateral, `2` if it is isosceles with exactly two equal sides, and `3` if all sides differ.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Multiples Of Exactly One
description: Return how many integers from `1` to `n` are divisible by exactly one of `a` and `b` (not by both).

title: Closest Multiple Of M
description: Return the multiple of `m` that is closest to `n`. If two multiples are equally close, return the larger one.

title: Points Inside Radius
description: `p` lists points as flat pairs `x, y`. Return how many points lie within or on the circle of radius `r` centred at the origin.

title: Rectangles Containing Point
description: `rects` lists axis-aligned rectangles as flat groups `x1, y1, x2, y2` with `x1 <= x2` and `y1 <= y2`. Return how many rectangles contain the point `(px, py)`, borders included.
constraints: 4 <= rects.length <= 1000 and rects.length is a multiple of 4

title: Checkerboard Sum Difference
description: `g` is a table stored row by row with `cols` columns. Colour cell `(row, col)` dark when `row + col` is even and light otherwise. Return (sum of dark cells) minus (sum of light cells).
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 1000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Diagonally Dominant Check
description: `g` is a square table (`cols` rows and `cols` columns) stored row by row. Return `true` if in every row the absolute value of the diagonal cell is strictly greater than the sum of the absolute values of the other cells of that row.
constraints: g.length equals cols * cols and 1 <= cols <= 31

title: Lower Triangular Check
description: `g` is a square table (`cols` rows and `cols` columns) stored row by row. Return `true` if every cell above the main diagonal is `0`.
constraints: g.length equals cols * cols and 1 <= cols <= 31

title: Symmetric Matrix Check
description: `g` is a square table (`cols` rows and `cols` columns) stored row by row. Return `true` if the table equals its own transpose, that is `g[r][c] == g[c][r]` for all cells.
constraints: g.length equals cols * cols and 1 <= cols <= 31

title: Sorted Rows Count
description: `g` is a table stored row by row with `cols` columns. Return how many rows are in non-decreasing order from left to right.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 1000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Column With Largest Sum
description: `g` is a table stored row by row with `cols` columns. Return the index of the column with the largest sum (the smallest index on a tie).
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 1000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Longest Same Parity Run
description: Return the length of the longest block of consecutive elements of `a` that are all even or all odd.

title: Most Minus Least Common Letter
description: Among the letters that appear in `s`, find the one used most often and the one used least often. Return the difference between these two counts.

title: Longest Stretch Without Letter
description: Return the length of the longest block of consecutive characters of `s` that does not contain the letter `c` (`c` is a single lowercase letter; the answer is `0` when `s` consists only of `c`).
constraints: s has only lowercase letters and c is one lowercase letter

title: Subarrays With Exactly K Distinct
description: Return the number of contiguous parts of `a` that contain exactly `k` different values, modulo `1000000007`. Parts at different positions count separately even when their contents are equal.

title: Reverse Pairs Count
description: Return the number of pairs of indices `i < j` with `a[i] > 2 * a[j]`, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Range Sum Count
description: Return the number of contiguous non-empty parts of `a` whose sum lies in the range `[lo, hi]` (both ends included), modulo `1000000007`.

title: Nested Envelopes Chain
description: `dims` lists envelopes as flat pairs `(width, height)`. One envelope fits inside another only if both its width and its height are strictly smaller. Envelopes cannot be rotated. Return the largest number of envelopes that can be nested one inside the next.

examples.explanation: At most 3 envelopes can be nested.
At most 1 envelopes can be nested.

title: Balloon Burst Max Coins
description: `a[i]` is the number written on balloon `i`. Bursting balloon `i` gives `left * a[i] * right` coins, where `left` and `right` are the numbers of its current neighbours (a missing neighbour counts as `1`). The neighbours update after every burst. Return the largest total number of coins you can collect by bursting all balloons in the best order.

title: Merge Stones Min Cost
description: There is a row of piles of stones `a`. One move merges exactly `k` consecutive piles into one pile, and the cost of the move is the total number of stones in those `k` piles. Return the smallest total cost to end with a single pile, or `-1` if that is impossible.

title: Regular Expression Match
description: Decide whether the whole string `s` matches the pattern `p`. In `p`, `.` matches any single character, and `x*` (a letter or `.` followed by `*`) matches zero or more copies of that element. The match must cover all of `s`.
constraints: s has lowercase letters; p has lowercase letters, `.` and `*`, and every `*` follows a letter or `.`

title: Distinct Subsequences Total
description: Return the number of different non-empty strings that can be obtained as a subsequence of `s`, modulo `1000000007`. A subsequence keeps the original order of the chosen letters.

title: Strongly Connected Components Count
description: A directed graph has nodes `0..n-1` and edges given as flat pairs `(from, to)` in `edges`. Two nodes belong to the same strongly connected component if each can reach the other by following edge directions. Return the number of strongly connected components.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= edges.length <= 200000 and edges.length is even

title: Maximum Network Flow
description: A directed network has nodes `0..n-1`. `edges` lists pipes as flat triples `(from, to, capacity)`; each pipe carries at most its capacity from `from` to `to`, and several pipes may join the same nodes. Return the largest amount that can be sent from node `s` to node `t` when the amount entering every other node equals the amount leaving it.
constraints: 2 <= n <= 1000 and edges.length is a multiple of 3 and edges.length <= 6000
0 <= from, to < n, 0 <= capacity <= 1000 and s != t

title: Egg Drop Minimum Trials
description: You have `eggs` identical eggs and a building with floors `1..floors`. There is an unknown critical floor `x` (`0 <= x <= floors`): an egg dropped from a floor `<= x` survives (and can be reused), and one dropped from a floor `> x` breaks. Return the smallest number of drops that is enough to determine `x` for sure in the worst case.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of drops is 2.
The minimum number of drops is 3.

title: Strange Printer Turns
description: A printer can print a row of one repeated letter in a single turn, starting and ending at any positions, and it overwrites whatever was printed there before. Return the smallest number of turns needed to print the string `s` on an initially blank strip.

title: Rain Water In Heightmap
description: `g` is a height map stored row by row with `cols` columns. Rain falls evenly and water can flow off the map across any border cell; water in a cell can flow to its four neighbours only if they are not higher than the water level. Return the total volume of water that stays trapped after the rain ends.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Three Windows Best Total
description: Choose three non-overlapping groups of exactly `k` consecutive elements of `a`. Return the largest possible total of the three groups.

title: Longest Increasing Path In Grid
description: `g` is a grid of integers stored row by row with `cols` columns. Starting from any cell you may move up, down, left or right to a neighbouring cell with a strictly larger value, any number of times. Return the largest number of cells on such a path.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Return the shortest substring of `s` that contains every character of `t` at least as many times as it occurs in `t`. If several substrings have the shortest length, return the leftmost one. Return the empty string if no substring qualifies.
constraints: s and t contain only lowercase letters

title: Signed Sum Ways
description: Put a `+` or a `-` sign in front of every element of `a` and add them up. Return the number of sign choices whose total equals `target`. Choices that differ in the sign of at least one position are different, even when the elements are equal.

title: Distinct Palindromic Subsequences
description: Return the number of different non-empty strings that are palindromes and appear as a subsequence of `s`, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: s has only the letters a, b, c and d

title: Best Submatrix Sum Under Cap
description: `g` is a table stored row by row with `cols` columns. Over all rectangular blocks of consecutive rows and columns, find the one with the largest sum that does not exceed `K`, and return that sum. A block with sum at most `K` is guaranteed to exist.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 1000 and g.length is a multiple of cols
-100 <= g[i] <= 100 and -100000 <= K <= 100000, and some block has sum at most K

title: Three Column Colourings Count
description: Colour every cell of a grid with `n` rows and `3` columns using one of three colours so that no two cells sharing a side have the same colour. Return the number of valid colourings, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Cheapest Point Network
description: `points` lists locations as flat pairs `(x, y)`. Connecting two points by a cable costs the Manhattan distance `|x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|`. Return the smallest total cable cost that connects all points together (directly or through other points).

title: Islands After Each Addition Total
description: An `R x C` map starts as all water. `positions` lists cells as flat pairs `(row, col)`; they are turned into land one at a time in the given order (a cell that is already land stays land). After each step, count the islands, where an island is a maximal group of land cells connected through up/down/left/right neighbours. Return the sum of these counts over all steps.

examples.explanation: The island counts add up to 8.
The island counts add up to 1.

constraints: 1 <= R, C <= 100 and 2 <= positions.length <= 20000 and positions.length is even

title: Narrowest Range Covering All Lists
description: Several non-decreasing lists are stored one after another in `vals`; `lens[i]` is the length of the `i`-th list. A range `[lo, hi]` covers a list if at least one of its elements lies inside the range. Return the smallest possible value of `hi - lo` over all ranges that cover every list.
constraints: 1 <= lens.length <= 3500, every lens[i] >= 1 and the lens add up to vals.length <= 100000
-1000000 <= vals[i] <= 1000000 and each list is in non-decreasing order

title: Take From Either End Gap
description: Two players take turns, the first player moving first. On a turn the player removes either the leftmost or the rightmost number of the row `a` and adds it to their own score. Both players play to maximise their own final score. Return the first player's final score minus the second player's final score.

title: Permutations With K Inversions
description: An inversion of a permutation `p` of `1..n` is a pair of positions `i < j` with `p[i] > p[j]`. Return the number of permutations of `1..n` that have exactly `k` inversions, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Candy Rounds To Empty
description: `a[i]` candies lie in pile `i`. In each round, the `k` largest non-empty piles (all non-empty piles if fewer than `k` exist) each lose exactly one candy. Return the number of rounds needed until every pile is empty.

title: Cancelling Neighbours Left
description: Repeatedly choose two neighbouring elements of `a` whose sum is `0` and delete both (the elements around them become neighbours). Continue until no such pair remains. Return the number of elements left; this number does not depend on which pairs you choose.

title: Rotation Start With Nonnegative Prefixes
description: You may start reading the circular array `a` at any index `s` and then read `n` elements going right (wrapping around). Return the smallest `s` for which every running total during this reading is `>= 0`, or `-1` if no start works.

title: Prefix Reach Total
description: For a target `q`, let its answer be the smallest `L` such that the first `L` elements of `a` sum to at least `q`, or `a.length + 1` if no prefix is large enough. Return the sum of the answers of all targets in `queries`, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The answers add up to 10 modulo 1000000007.
The answers add up to 1 modulo 1000000007.

title: Longest Span Under Range Budget
description: Return the length of the longest contiguous part of `a` whose largest element minus its smallest element is at most `k`.

title: Shortest Window With Quota
description: Return the length of the shortest contiguous part of `a` that contains at least `c` elements that are `>= t`, or `-1` if no such part exists.

title: Prefix Leader Changes
description: For every prefix of `a`, its leader is the value that occurs strictly more often than every other value in that prefix; a prefix has no leader when two or more values tie for the highest count. Walk through the prefixes of lengths `1, 2, ..., n` and return how many times the leader status (a value, or no leader) differs from that of the previous prefix.

title: Nearest Smaller Distance Total
description: For each index `i`, let its distance be the number of positions to the nearest element anywhere in `a` (left or right) that is strictly smaller than `a[i]`; the distance is `0` if no element is smaller. Return the sum of all distances modulo `1000000007`.

title: Insertions To Cap Gaps
description: You may insert any integers into `a`. After sorting, the difference between every two neighbouring values must be at most `d`. Return the smallest number of integers to insert.

title: Smallest Maximum Pair Sum
description: `a` has an even number of elements. Split it into pairs (each element in exactly one pair). The score of a split is the largest sum of a pair. Return the smallest possible score.

title: Longest Span Few Vowels
description: Return the length of the longest substring of `s` that contains at most `k` vowels (`a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u`).

title: Square Substring Count
description: A square is a non-empty string of the form `ww` (some string repeated twice). Count the pairs `(i, L)` such that the substring of `s` starting at index `i` with length `2L` is a square. Equal substrings found at different positions count separately.

title: Subsequence Occurrences Count
description: Count the ways to pick positions `i1 < i2 < ... < im` of `s` (where `m = t.length`) so that the characters picked, read in order, spell `t`. Ways that use different position sets count separately. Return the count modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: s and t have only lowercase letters

title: Least Rotation Start
description: Writing `s` as a circle, a rotation starting at index `i` reads `s[i..] + s[..i-1]`. Return the smallest index `i` whose rotation is lexicographically smallest among all rotations.

examples.explanation: The smallest rotation starts at index 2.
The smallest rotation starts at index 0.

title: Nested Repeat Decoded Length
description: `s` is encoded as follows: `k[x]` means the decoded form of `x` repeated `k` times, and letters stand for themselves; encodings can be nested and concatenated, for example `2[a3[bc]]d` decodes to `abcbcbcabcbcbcd`. Return the length of the decoded string modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: s is a valid encoding using lowercase letters, digits and brackets; every repeat count is between 1 and 1000 and every bracket pair is non-empty

title: Fewest Keystrokes With Caps Lock
description: You type `s` on a keyboard. Caps Lock starts off. Pressing a letter key writes it in lowercase when Caps Lock is off and in uppercase when it is on (1 keystroke). Pressing a letter together with Shift writes the opposite case (2 keystrokes). Pressing the Caps Lock key switches its state (1 keystroke). Return the fewest keystrokes needed to produce `s` exactly.
constraints: s has only lowercase and uppercase letters

title: Wildcard Fill No Repeats
description: `s` consists of the letters `a`, `b`, `c` and wildcards `?`, and no two neighbouring fixed letters are equal. Replace every `?` by `a`, `b` or `c` so that no two neighbouring characters are equal, and return the lexicographically smallest string you can get.

examples.explanation: The smallest valid string is acb.
The smallest valid string is a.

constraints: s has only a, b, c and ?; no two adjacent non-? characters are equal

title: Largest Letter Subsequence
description: Among all non-empty subsequences of `s` (letters kept in their original order), return the lexicographically largest one.

title: Trailing Ones Total
description: The trailing-ones count of a positive integer is the number of consecutive `1` bits at the end of its binary form (for `6 = 110` it is `0`, for `7 = 111` it is `3`). Return the sum of the trailing-ones counts of all integers from `1` to `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Even Parity Count Upto N
description: A number has even parity if its binary form contains an even number of `1` bits (`0` counts as even). Return how many integers `x` with `0 <= x <= n` have even parity.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Consecutive Sum Representations
description: Return in how many ways `n` can be written as the sum of two or more consecutive positive integers (for example `9 = 4 + 5 = 2 + 3 + 4`, so the answer for `9` is `2`).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Last Digit Power Sum
description: The last digit of `i^e` is `(i^e) mod 10`. Return the sum of the last digits of `1^e, 2^e, ..., n^e`, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Integer Triangles With Perimeter
description: Return the number of different triangles with positive area whose three side lengths are positive integers adding up to `n`. Triangles that differ only by the order of the sides are the same triangle.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Digit Sum Total Upto N
description: Return the sum of the decimal digit sums of all integers from `1` to `n`, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: No Equal Neighbouring Digits Count
description: Return how many integers from `1` to `n` have no two neighbouring digits that are equal in their decimal form (for example `121` qualifies, `122` does not).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Sum Of Remainders Upto N
description: Return the sum of `n mod i` for every `i` from `1` to `n`, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Snake Game Replay Score
description: A snake lives on an `R x C` board and starts as a single cell at row `0`, column `0`. `moves` lists directions: `0` up, `1` right, `2` down, `3` left. `food` lists food cells as flat pairs `row, col`; only the first uneaten food is on the board at any time. Each move places a new head in the neighbouring cell. If the head leaves the board the game ends. If the new head lands on the food, the snake grows by one cell (the tail stays) and the score rises by one, and the next food appears; otherwise the tail cell is removed. If the new head then lies on any other cell of the snake the game ends. Return `-1` if the game ends during the moves, otherwise the final score.
constraints: 1 <= R, C <= 100 and the food pairs lie on the board

title: Browser History Replay Total
description: A browser starts on page `0` with no other history. `ops` lists operations as flat pairs `(type, value)`: type `0` visits page `value` (this erases all forward history), type `1` goes back `value` steps (stopping at the oldest page), and type `2` goes forward `value` steps (stopping at the newest page). Return the sum of the current page numbers observed after each operation, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The page numbers add up to 24.
The page numbers add up to 0.

title: Undo Redo Replay Total
description: A counter starts at `0`. `ops` lists operations as flat pairs `(type, value)`. Type `0` adds `value` to the counter and erases the redo history. Type `1` undoes the most recent applied addition (subtracting it again) and does nothing if there is none; the `value` is ignored. Type `2` redoes the most recently undone addition and does nothing if there is none; the `value` is ignored. Return the sum of the counter values observed after each operation, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The counter values add up to 26.
The counter values add up to 0.

title: Hotel Room Assignment Total
description: A hotel has unlimited rooms numbered `1, 2, 3, ...`. `bookings` lists stays as flat pairs `(start, end)` sorted by `start`, with `start < end`. Each stay is put into the lowest-numbered room that is free at time `start` (a room whose previous stay ends at a time `<= start` is free). Return the sum of the room numbers assigned to all stays, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The room numbers add up to 5.
The room numbers add up to 1.

constraints: 0 <= start < end <= 1000000000 and starts are in non-decreasing order

title: Rumour Spread Days
description: `g` is a grid stored row by row with `cols` columns; `1` is an open cell and `0` is a wall. On day `0` the rumour is known on the open cells listed in `starts` (flat pairs `row, col`). Every day it moves from each informed cell to its open neighbours (up, down, left, right). Return the number of days until every open cell knows it, or `-1` if some open cell is never reached.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 1000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; every g[i] is 0 or 1
1 <= starts.length <= 1000, even, and every start is an open cell

title: Largest Region After Opening One Wall
description: `g` is a grid stored row by row with `cols` columns; `1` is an open cell and `0` is a wall. A region is a maximal set of open cells connected through up/down/left/right moves. You may turn at most one wall into an open cell. Return the largest region size you can obtain.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 1000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; every g[i] is 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Fewest Walls To Break
description: `g` is a grid stored row by row with `cols` columns; `1` is a wall and `0` is a free cell. You walk from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell moving up, down, left or right. Every wall cell you step on (including the start and end cells) must be broken. Return the smallest number of walls you must break.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; every g[i] is 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Cells Reachable Within Budget
description: `g` is a grid of non-negative entry costs stored row by row with `cols` columns. You start on the top-left cell (its own cost is not paid) and move up, down, left or right; stepping onto a cell costs its value. Return how many cells (including the start) can be reached with a total cost of at most `B`.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: First Connected Day
description: There are `n` cities `0..n-1` and no roads. `roads` lists new roads as flat pairs `(u, v)`; the `i`-th pair (counting from `1`) is built on day `i`. Return the first day on which every city can reach every other city by roads, `0` if `n` is `1`, or `-1` if that never happens.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= roads.length <= 200000 and roads.length is even

title: Two-Hop Reach Count
description: An undirected graph has nodes `0..n-1` and edges given as flat pairs in `edges`. Return how many nodes other than `s` can be reached from `s` using at most two edges.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= edges.length <= 200000 and edges.length is even

title: Subtrees With Target Sum
description: A rooted tree has nodes `0..n-1` with `n = par.length + 1` and root `0`; node `i + 1` has parent `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`). Node `u` holds the value `vals[u]`. Return how many nodes have a subtree (the node and all its descendants) whose values add up to exactly `t`.

title: Longest Increasing Downward Path
description: A rooted tree has nodes `0..n-1` with `n = par.length + 1` and root `0`; node `i + 1` has parent `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`). Node `u` holds `vals[u]`. A downward path goes from a node to one of its descendants through parent-to-child steps. Return the largest number of nodes on a downward path whose values are strictly increasing.

examples.explanation: The longest increasing path has 4 nodes.

title: Saddle Cell Count
description: `g` is a table stored row by row with `cols` columns. A cell is a saddle cell if its value is at most every other value in its row and at least every other value in its column (equal values are allowed). Return the number of saddle cells.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Longest Line Of Ones
description: `g` is a grid of `0` and `1` stored row by row with `cols` columns. Return the length of the longest straight line of consecutive `1` cells, where the line may run horizontally, vertically, along a diagonal, or along an anti-diagonal.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; every g[i] is 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges
